To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
breast cancer aggregates in families of patients suffering from breast cancer in a site-specific and non-site specific fashion.

breast cancer is the leading tumor in families of breast cancer patients, that the Li-Fraumani/SBLA-symptom is the most common tumor disease after breast cancer and that the familial adenocarcintomatosis (Lynch II) occurs as the second most common tumor disease.
the occurrence of breast cancer in a family is a risk factor for the occurrence of breast and other cancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects of familial breast cancer: 1) The familial occurrence of breast cancer in relation to other neoplasias, in particular to those of the colon, endometrium, ovaries and the skin.
the identification and characterization of genes that are involved in breast cancer and other tumors, and that may also play an important role in normal development.

the following topics: (1) the occurrence of the different tumor diseases in the families of breast cancer patients, (2) the familial aggregation of breast cancer, and (3) the occurrence of breast cancer and other tumor diseases in the same families.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in the families of the breast cancer patients the following malignancies are more frequent: breast carcinoma, colorectal carcinoma, ovarian cancer, endometrial cancer, uterine leiomyoma, sarcoma and brain tumors.
the familial aggregation of breast cancer and the occurrence of the Li-Frumanemi/SBLA-symptomatology are two independent events.
the Li-Fraumei/SBLA syndrome is a very rare disease, which is not to be confused with the more frequent familial adenocarcino-matosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Li-Fraumani/SBLA-syn- drome is not a rare disease in the families of breast cancer patients and that the Li-Fr aumeni-syndrome may be the common denominator for the familial adenocarcini- mata- sis and the Li-Frannieni/SBLA syndrome.

the breast cancer patients in the present study were found to have an increased incidence of cancer in general and of cancer of the ovary, uterus and colon, and a decreased incidence of cancer of the cervix uteri.
the Li-Fraumemi-syndrome is a very rare condition in families of breast cancer patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Li-Fraumani syndrome and SBLA syndrome are not synonymous, and the Li-Faumani syndrome has a broader spectrum of tumors than the SBLA syndrome.
there are two different syndromes with a strong familial aggregation of breast cancer and that the breast cancer risk in women with a family history of breast cancer is not the same in all families.
